title: Enterprise Adoption Accelerator - First 180 Days Ops Guide
author: Maya Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook defines a cross-functional, prescriptive operations guide to accelerate enterprise customer adoption during the first 180 days after provision. It is designed for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), Platform Engineering, and SRE to coordinate a predictable path from provisioning -> stability -> value realization -> QBR.

Scope:
- Applies to Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem) enterprise customers where Redwood provides onboarding support.
- Covers technical readiness, SLO/SLA alignment, telemetry gating, cost controls, training, and QBR preparation.
- Not a substitute for customer-specific legal or compliance requirements; use security gates documented in the enterprise compliance checklist.

Quick summary of phases:
1) Pre-provisioning (Days -14 to 0)
2) Provision & Cutover (Days 0–7)
3) Stabilize & Harden (Days 8–45)
4) Optimize & Expand (Days 46–120)
5) QBR Prep & Handoff (Days 121–180)

Owners & contacts:
- CS Lead: Maya Patel (owner)
- SE: Jordan Lee
- Platform Oncall: Carlos Mendoza
- Customer Dev Lead: <customer-contact>
- Security Gatekeeper: Priya Nair

Phase 0 — Pre-provisioning checklist (Days -14 to 0)
- Verify contract/tenant ID and region mapping with Finance (billing code).
- Confirm required networking (VPC peering, firewall rules), collect CIDR ranges, and exchange IP allowlists.
- Validate KMS/HSM integration requirements and key policies.
- Review model catalog and pin initial model families (e.g., rdx-7b-q4f) with customer for predictability.
- Create a shared runbook document in the customer repo and populate the following variables: tenant_id, contact_emails, escalation_phone, expected_peak_rps.

Pre-provisioning gating criteria (must pass before cutover):
- Networking test OK (ingress + egress)
- Auth provisioning validated (SAML/SCIM or API-key test)
- Telemetry contract agreed (metrics and traces endpoints)

Phase 1 — Provision & Cutover (Days 0–7)
Primary goals: successful traffic cutover with safety nets and initial verification of SLIs.
Key steps (ordered):
1. Provision tenant with reserved capacity or private control-plane configuration.
2. Run automated ingress smoke tests (see snippet below).
3. Enable monitoring hooks (per-route tracing, token-level billing stream) and confirm metrics flow.
4. Perform two staged traffic shifts: 5% -> 30% -> 100% (wait 30–60m between stages).
5. Execute customer acceptance tests (happy-path prompts and latency checks).

Example smoke-test curl command:

curl -X POST https://ingress.customer.example/api/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TEST_KEY>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"rdx-7b-q4f","input":"Hello, smoke test"}'

Acceptance criteria for cutover:
- 95th percentile latency within agreed SLO (example: p95 < 250ms for short prompts)
- Error rate < 0.5% for 30m after 100% traffic shift
- Token billing counters reported and reconciled with billing view

Phase 2 — Stabilize & Harden (Days 8–45)
Objectives: resolve early regressions, tune batching/kv cache, and enforce cost guardrails.
Stability checklist:
- Deploy per-tenant retry/backoff configuration (adaptive retry policy)
- Confirm KV cache warmup for conversational workloads (cache hit rate target >= 60% within 24h)
- Validate autoscaling behavior under a 2x synthetic spike (runload simulator ID: loadgen-1801)
- Apply rate limits and quota thresholds with notification hooks to CS and customer dev team
- Schedule a mid-30-day technical health review with SRE + CS + SE

Known categories of early failures and mitigation (examples):
- Symptom: Sudden p50/p95 spike after model change
  - Immediate action: rollback to pinned model in control plane (owner: SE).
- Symptom: High token usage unexpectedly
  - Immediate action: enable soft throttle and trigger cost alert to customer and CS.
- Symptom: KV cache miss storm after restart
  - Immediate action: gradual ramp and pre-warm cache, adjust caching TTLs.

Phase 3 — Optimize & Expand (Days 46–120)
Focus: tuning for unit economics and broader feature adoption.
Tactics:
- Run prompt suite evals against production traffic sample to identify hallucination regressions.
- Suggest quantization/variant recommendations for cost-sensitive routes and validate quality impact on eval sets.
- Implement batching and request coalescing for high-throughput endpoints (target average tokens/req).
- Introduce model fanout for non-latency-critical workflows (lower-cost variants).

Optional experiments (A/B):
- Canary a q4f quantized variant on 10% traffic for 14 days, collect quality metrics via eval harness.
- Test prefix caching on highest-volume customer route and measure token savings.

Phase 4 — QBR Prep & Handoff (Days 121–180)
Deliverables:
- Compile QBR packet including: availability, latency, model performance (evals), cost breakdown (token usage by route), adoption milestones, and roadmap asks.
- Actionable items: 1–3 prioritized ops or product changes with owners and due dates.
- Handoff checklist: transfer technical ownership to customer success long-term owner and document runbook escalation links.

QBR metrics mapping (recommended):
| Customer outcome | Internal metric | Threshold / target |
|---|---|---|
| Responsiveness | p95 latency / route | < agreed SLO (e.g., 250ms) |
| Reliability | Error rate / day | < 0.5% |
| Cost efficiency | tokens per useful response | reduce by >= 10% vs baseline |
| Consistency | eval regression rate | 0 critical regressions |

Telemetry & gating rules
- Minimum telemetry to validate adoption: per-request latency histogram, token counts, model-version tags, and trace ID.
- Telemetry retention for the onboarding period: 90 days by default (longer for enterprise upon request).
- Gating rule examples:
  - If p95 latency increases > 40% over baseline for 1h -> auto-scale and notify SRE/CS.
  - If token cost delta > 25% week-over-week -> trigger cost governance review.

Escalation matrix (technical)
- Tier 1 (CS/SE triage, 15-minute response): CS Lead + Assigned SE
- Tier 2 (Platform SRE, 30-minute response): Platform Oncall (Carlos Mendoza)
- Tier 3 (Engineering & Exec notification, 60-minute response): Eng Platform Lead + CS Director

Communication templates (examples)
- Customer ops update subject line: "[Redwood] Week 2 – Cutover Health & Next Steps"
- Short status template (use in Slack/email):
  - Summary: 2-sentence overview of current state
  - Key metrics: p95 latency, error rate, token burn delta
  - Actions this week: 3 bullets with owners

Security & compliance checklist (minimum for go-live)
1. Confirm SAML user provisioning and least-privilege roles implemented.
2. Verify TLS termination location and certificate rotation policies.
3. Confirm KMS integration and key access audit events are flowing to the customer audit collector.
4. Run a scoped data residency verification test (if customer requires).

Cost-control guardrails
- Configure soft quotas per-route and per-tenant with automated notifications to CS and the customer budget owner.
- Enable token burn anomaly detection; default threshold 2.5x baseline within 24h -> auto-throttle to 20% and open investigation ticket.
- Recommend monthly cost review cadence during first 3 months.

Training & enablement plan
- Week 1: Developer ramp-up workshop (1 hour) — example prompts, rate limit behaviors, telemetry dashboards.
- Week 4: Runbook walkthrough and incident simulation (game-day).
- Week 8: Product feature enablement session (integrations, caching knobs, model tuning).

Runbook snippets & automation examples
- Safe rollback CLI example:
  redwoodctl tenant rollback --tenant-id <TENANT> --model rdx-7b-q4f --to-version 2026-02-01

- Telemetry query example (PromQL-like pseudo-query):
  sum(rate(redwood_request_errors_total[5m])) by (tenant) / sum(rate(redwood_requests_total[5m])) by (tenant)

Escalation play examples
1. If error rate > 1% sustained for 20m: notify CS, pause non-critical batched jobs, and open high-priority incident.
2. If p95 latency > SLO * 1.5 for 30m: enable emergency autoscale, rollback recent model change, and notify eng oncall.

Postmortem & continuous improvement
- At the end of the 180-day engagement, produce a joint retrospective with the customer including: incident log, cost delta analysis, feature adoption report, and 3 prioritized improvements.
- Keep a living action register (shared doc) and track closure within QBRs.

Appendix: Templates and checklists
- Provision readiness table (sample):
| Item | Owner | Status |
| Networking (VPC peering) | Customer NetOps | DONE |
| KMS access | Security Gatekeeper | PENDING |
| Initial model pin | SE | DONE |

- Customer acceptance test (short list):
  1) Submit 100 short inference requests and verify p95 < SLO
  2) Submit a 1000-token document generation and verify stability under load
  3) Verify billing events appear in token stream ingestion
